text.p: These are significant stories in the Nigerian press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Fuel scarcity worsens in commercial capital, Lagos, as state-run Nigerian National Petroleum Corporation and petroleum marketing companies blaming each other for the shortage.
- Central Bank says any merchant bank wishing to expand into commercial banking will first have to increase its paid-up capital to 500 million naira.
- Nigerian banks are trying to fathom new ways of retaining depositors, as increased liquidity forces down interest rates.
- The Manufacturers Association of Nigeria's Export Group predicts an increase in non-oil exports following government's review of the Export Expansion Grant in the 1997 budget.
- Central Bank lifts official restrictions on hard currency allowances for Nigerians travelling abroad.
- Police chief reports slow progress on investigations into a number of assassinations.

- Chairman of the National Economic Intelligence Committee, Sam Aluko, has suggested that a realistic exchange rate for the naira would be 50 naira to the dollar, instead of the current 80 naira to the dollar.
- U.S. police have arrested a top official of Mobil Corp.'s Nigeria unit in connection with an $800,000 fraud at the Oso/NGL Condensate project.
- Britain's Virgin Atlantic Airways may acquire a 40 percent block share in Nigeria Airways. Sources at the Presidency confirmed the deal had been given the go-ahead at the highest level.
